comment: Tests allowed to fail once and pass on retry without failing the job. Everything else that flakes fails CI. This list is debt: each entry is a test that is lying about the product, and it should shrink, never grow. Adding an entry is a deliberate decision that needs a reason and a date, not a way to get a red build green.

allow.test: channel-browser.spec.ts › Enter with no matches jumps to create
allow.why: Pre-existing at the audit that added this gate. Not yet diagnosed.

allow.test: composer-image-draw.spec.ts › spoiler marking survives drawing on the attachment
allow.why: Pre-existing at the audit that added this gate. Not yet diagnosed.

allow.test: composer-selection-formatting.spec.ts › Ordered list starts at a collapsed caret on a new line
allow.why: Pre-existing at the audit that added this gate. Not yet diagnosed.

allow.test: messaging.spec.ts › sends a thread message to its parent channel with a root-thread link
allow.why: NOT a timeout-budget flake, and this entry exists to record that. It was allowlisted once on 2026-08-17 on the theory that it shared the 5000ms default expect budget with two other flakes. Raising the budget to 15s fixed those two and did nothing here: on this pull request's own CI it failed again with 'Timeout 15000ms exceeded while waiting on the predicate' at messaging.spec.ts:2010, then passed on retry. The poll waits for a thread reply sent to its parent channel to appear in that channel's timeline; sharedRow never enters the DOM. That is a real intermittent race in the send-to-channel path, product or harness, and it matches this test's history: the header comment of scripts/summarize-flaky-tests.mjs cites it as reason #1 the gate exists, after it passed on retry on a run that green-lit a promotion candidate and then failed three attempts in a row three hours later. Do not raise a timeout to close this. Pull the trace and video from a failed attempt and find why the row never renders.
